pr_title: Accurately reflect the canonical casing of `API-Version` and `OS-Type` headers
pr_body:
Go automatically canonicalises HTTP headers, meaning the string `API-Version` passed as a header has always been returned as `Api-Version`. Similarly, `OSType` is returned as `Ostype`.

This commit updates the documentation to reflect this behaviour and modifies the codebase to ensure that input strings are aligned with their canonical output values.

```markdown changelog
Update docs and code to reflect Go’s automatic canonicalisation of Api-Version and Ostype headers.
```

Closes: https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/49046#issuecomment-2525113278

issue_context.title: API docs incorrectly suggest the api version header is not canonicalised: `API-Version`
issue_context.body:
### Description

The `ping` endpoint docs suggest the api version response header is:

`API-Version`

It is in fact canonical:

```
curl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock -i http://localhost/_ping
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Api-Version: 1.44
```

`Api-Version` is the correct canonical format that headers should use and the docs could be updated to reflect this.

https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.44/#tag/System/operation/SystemVersion

### Reproduce

Check the docs 

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### docker version

```bash
1.44
```

### docker info

```bash
N/a
```

### Additional Info

_No response_
comments:
Hm, nice catch; yes, it looks like it's set as `API-Version`, but it's using go's stdlib header functionality which does the normalizing;
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/68dbb8b3859eed92ad3c52c25ca5bc2f7be181b9/api/server/middleware/version.go#L69-L71

Technically, this should not directly impact users, as these [must be handled case-insensitive](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc822#section-3.4.7), but  I had a quick peek if this was changed recently, because if that was the case we may have wanted to revert that to use non-canonical format in case there were implementations considering it to be case-sensitive.

Looks like the same applies to the `OSType` header, but I see that one waa added in https://github.com/moby/moby/commit/7199522ea2e77c77bf931474eca92aa502ce0031, but never documented (looks like that should be corrected as well).

Contributions welcome though if someone's interested to work on this;

- swagger can be found here; https://github.com/moby/moby/tree/master/api
- and versioned copies (used for documentation); https://github.com/moby/moby/tree/master/docs/api

But if we change, it would probably be good to also reference those in the correct format in code to prevent confusion, e.g. places like https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/68dbb8b3859eed92ad3c52c25ca5bc2f7be181b9/api/server/middleware/version_test.go#L143-L144

review_comments:
For others  reviewing; I suggested changing these to match the normalised  version.  Effectively these  parts of the change are a "no-op", but explicitly setting the headers in  the normalised form (instead of them implicitly being normalised by Go stdlib) reduces confusion.

As a follow-up to this PR I want to have  a  peek if we could define consts for this  (on which we could document why they're capitalised as they are), but I have not yet looked at the impact of that (i.e.; where to best put the const without that resulting in cumbersome imports / inter-package dependencies).
